The project has changed what is retained about a population, rather than positing a new force or claiming a new physical realization.

The resulting research program is therefore internal to mathematics at this stage. It studies a hierarchy of marked populations, their inverse problems, exact computation, and arithmetic singularities after a precisely defined Euler lift. Older physical, commercial, or external ambitions neither prove its significance nor limit the objects it can now examine. The useful inheritance is the ability to calculate exact populations, distinguish insufficient representations, and move consistently between valuation, lattice and conductor descriptions. The new work must earn its further claims through theorems or explicit counterexamples about the height hierarchy itself.

One further lesson from the archive is that a change of coefficient domain and a change of question are separate moves. Exact cyclotomic arithmetic can certify a finite phase sum that floating-point recognition only suggests. Exact integer arithmetic can certify the histogram of a large finite population. Neither act automatically changes what the histogram measures. A perfectly certified binary census remains a binary census. The co-binary example makes that point without relying on measurement noise, numerical instability, unverified physical premises or imperfect training data: even exact binary information can be insufficient for an exact higher-height question.

Conversely, enlarging the question does not require abandoning the old exact arithmetic. The same graph can be studied through an integer coefficient table, a real parameter 0<q<10<q<1, a cyclotomic specialization, a cut-lattice theta series, or a Dirichlet series. Each view should carry an explicit account of the markers it retains. A statement about the full marked hierarchy cannot be replaced by a statement about one root-of-unity specialization. A statement about an Euler singularity cannot substitute for equality of every local coefficient. The creative move is the selection of the relational population, while the archival discipline supplies the maps that let its different views be compared honestly.

12 Exact computation, certificates, and reproducible experiments

12.1 What a computation is intended to establish

The computational object is a population of labeled integer assignments. For a simple graph G=(V,E)G=(V,E), with V={0,…,n−1}V=\{0,\ldots,n-1\}, an assignment a∈ℕna\in\mathbb N^n has volume v(a)=∑iaiv(a)=\sum_i a_i, energy EG(a)=∑{i,j}∈E(ai−aj)2E_G(a)=\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E}(a_i-a_j)^2, and span maxiai−miniai\max_i a_i-\min_i a_i. The local series is LG(x,q)=∑axv(a)qEG(a)L_G(x,q)=\sum_a x^{v(a)}q^{E_G(a)}. Computing through volume RR means computing every coefficient of every polynomial [xv]LG[x^v]L_G for 0≤v≤R0\le v\le R. It does not mean evaluating the series at a few floating-point points or recording only energies below a second cutoff. An additional energy cutoff is legitimate only when it is part of the declared output and its omitted region is explicit.

The distinction between labeled profiles and isomorphism classes is essential. Graph relabeling does not change the resulting polynomial, but assignments related by a graph automorphism remain distinct members of the population. Dividing counts by an automorphism-group order generally gives incorrect coefficients because stabilizers vary. Orbit enumeration can accelerate computation, provided each representative carries its exact orbit size. The first implementation should retain labeled assignments; a later orbit implementation should reproduce those counts before becoming a source of larger examples.

Finite coefficient equality is a finite claim. Equality through volume RR is evidence about a truncation and proves equality of that truncation. It does not prove equality of the full local series. Conversely, a single differing coefficient is a complete witness that two full series differ. The software should make this asymmetry visible in its result types: a discrepancy record is conclusive, whereas an unresolved collision retains its tested bound. A graph pair may be cospectral, binary-census equivalent, or equal through a stated volume without being equivalent for the relational height population.

12.2 A reference enumerator whose meaning is transparent

At a fixed volume vv, enumerate all weak compositions of vv into nn parts. There are exactly (v+n−1n−1)\binom{v+n-1}{n-1} such assignments when n>0n>0. For each tuple, calculate energy directly from the normalized edge list, then increment the corresponding integer histogram. Python integers suffice: coefficients are arbitrary-precision integers and no rounding is involved. A sparse dictionary indexed by energy is preferable to a dense array when the attainable energies occupy a small subset of their possible range. The mathematical definition, rather than an optimization, remains the specification of this enumerator.

An exact and useful bound is EG(a)≤Δ(G)v2E_G(a)\le\Delta(G)v^2 for nonnegative assignments of volume vv. Indeed, (ai−aj)2≤ai2+aj2(a_i-a_j)^2\le a_i^2+a_j^2, so the energy is at most ∑idiai2≤Δ∑iai2≤Δv2\sum_i d_i a_i^2\le\Delta\sum_i a_i^2\le\Delta v^2. Concentrating all volume at a vertex of maximum degree attains the bound. The bound therefore checks both data validity and the maximum polynomial degree. It is not a reason to allocate every intermediate degree. At zero volume, the unique assignment is zero and contributes one at energy zero.

The reference cost through RR is proportional to |E|(R+nn)|E|\binom{R+n}{n}, up to tuple-generation and integer-arithmetic costs. This follows from summing the weak-composition counts, not from an assumption that all energies are distinct. Memory is controlled by the number of nonzero histogram entries retained. Timings must report nn, |E||E|, RR, the number of assignments visited, histogram support sizes, interpreter version, and hardware. An isolated runtime without these quantities cannot distinguish a better algorithm from an easier instance.

12.3 Three independent representations of the same coefficients

Translation normalization supplies the first independent check. Write a=b+c𝟏a=b+c\mathbf1, where c=miniaic=\min_i a_i and minibi=0\min_i b_i=0. Energy is unchanged and volume increases by ncnc. Consequently BG=(1−xn)LGB_G=(1-x^n)L_G, where BGB_G counts minimum-zero profiles. A direct minimum-zero enumerator should agree with the coefficient subtraction Bv=Lv−Lv−nB_v=L_v-L_{v-n}, taking negative indices as zero. This tests a bijection and a polynomial operation against an independent predicate. It also catches the mistake of normalizing each connected component separately when the declared convention uses one global minimum.

The second representation uses nested level sets. For a normalized profile of span hh, put St={i:ai≥t}S_t=\{i:a_i\ge t\}. Then ⌀≠Sh⊆⋯⊆S1⊊V\varnothing\ne S_h\subseteq\cdots\subseteq S_1\subsetneq V, and repeated sets are permitted. Volume is ∑t|St|\sum_t|S_t|. Define Q(S,T)=∑{i,j}∈E(1S(i)−1S(j))(1T(i)−1T(j))Q(S,T)=\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E}(1_S(i)-1_S(j))(1_T(i)-1_T(j)). For T⊆ST\subseteq S, this is the number of edges between TT and V\SV\setminus S. Expanding a square gives

EG(a)=∑t=1h|δSt|+2∑1≤u<t≤hQ(Su,St). E_G(a)=\sum_{t=1}^{h}|\delta S_t|+2\sum_{1\le u<t\le h}Q(S_u,S_t).

A level-chain enumerator therefore has a genuinely different failure surface from a weak-composition enumerator. It should reconstruct the tuple as well as its three statistics and compare complete histograms. Omitting repetitions silently loses profiles with height gaps. Omitting the mixed terms silently replaces squared differences by absolute differences. These are mathematically different models, even when a few tiny examples happen to agree.

The fully marked series BG(x,q,z)B_G(x,q,z) retains span. Its span-one sector is exactly the nonconstant binary population: [z]BG=∑⌀≠S⊊Vx|S|q|δS|[z]B_G=\sum_{\varnothing\ne S\subsetneq V}x^{|S|}q^{|\delta S|}. This identifies a direct check against a bit-mask cut enumerator. The empty and full subsets require separate treatment in an unnormalized binary census. The marked identity proves that the full marked series contains the binary sector; setting z=1z=1 mixes sectors and does not establish a method for recovering them.

12.4 Exact polynomials before numerical evaluation

Each volume coefficient is stored as an integer polynomial in qq. Addition, multiplication, subtraction, and comparison use degree-indexed sparse maps. Rational coefficients are needed for logarithms, division of formal series, and Euler-factor extraction, so those operations use reduced fractions. A numerical value such as q=1/2q=1/2 is substituted only after the polynomial identity has been established. Equality at one rational point is weaker than polynomial equality; a discrepancy can also disappear at an exceptional specialization.

The two supplied graph pairs illustrate this discipline. The spectral pair has its first local discrepancy at volume two, with polynomial 2q2(1−q)3(1+q)2q^2(1-q)^3(1+q). The binary-census pair agrees in its complete binary population but first differs at volume three, with polynomial q3(1−q)(1−q3)2(1−q4)2q^3(1-q)(1-q^3)^2(1-q^4)^2. The corresponding values at one half are 3/323/32 and 11025/26214411025/262144. A release should retain expanded coefficient maps, factorizations, and exact substitutions. The factorization explains signs and exceptional endpoints; the expanded maps make recomputation straightforward. The factored expressions alone do not certify that every lower-volume coefficient was checked.

For connected graphs, the endpoint checks are particularly strong. At q=1q=1, the local series is (1−x)−n(1-x)^{-n}; at q=0q=0, only constant profiles survive, giving (1−xn)−1(1-x^n)^{-1}. Thus the normalized series becomes (1−xn)(1−x)−n(1-x^n)(1-x)^{-n} and 11, respectively. A disconnected graph has additional zero-energy profiles, so the connected endpoint formula must not be used as a universal assertion. Empty-edge graphs and isolated vertices are useful tests precisely because they expose hidden connectedness assumptions.

12.5 Ranking, unranking, and exact sampling

The finite population machinery can provide reproducible witnesses as well as totals. For fixed volume, order weak compositions lexicographically by labeled coordinates. Once a prefix is fixed, its unconstrained completion count is a binomial coefficient. Ranking sums counts of earlier possible next entries; unranking subtracts those counts until the selected branch is found. These operations establish an explicit bijection between assignments and integers in a known interval. A uniformly selected integer therefore gives an exactly uniform assignment, without floating-point probabilities.

Conditioning on energy or span requires completion counts for the conditioned population, not reuse of the unconstrained formula. A memoized state can retain the assigned boundary heights, remaining volume, accumulated energy, and any extrema required by the marking. Whenever an edge has both endpoints assigned, charge its energy once. The remaining state must retain every quantity on which future contributions depend. A compressed state justified only by empirical agreement is a heuristic until its completion-count equivalence is proved. Tree decompositions offer a principled route to smaller boundaries, but the correctness argument is still the same conditional partition of the original labeled population.

The released HeightPopulation implementation supports ranking for finite bounded classes whose completion counts are exact and independently checked. The round-trip identities unrank(rank(a))=a\operatorname{unrank}(\operatorname{rank}(a))=a and rank(unrank(j))=j\operatorname{rank}(\operatorname{unrank}(j))=j must hold over the complete small population. Sampling is useful for exploring typical profiles, but sampling cannot replace complete enumeration when the reported result is a full coefficient or an absence claim. Each sampled witness should include its rank, population size, seed provenance when applicable, and the exact conditioning predicate.

12.6 Certificates and the trusted boundary

The implemented certificate format is singularity.certificate/1. It records the finite graph source and its digest, the maximum retained volume, local coefficients, minimum-zero coefficients, fully marked coefficients, total enumerated profile count, and formal Euler exponents. Local integer counts are JSON integers. Exact rational polynomial data use triples [degree, numerator, denominator] with integer entries and a positive denominator. The released Python reader preserves these integers exactly. A JavaScript transport should convert large counts to decimal strings or BigInt before arithmetic, because ordinary JavaScript numbers do not preserve integers beyond 253−12^{53}-1; that transport change is a future schema extension rather than a property of the current format.

A pair certificate adds the second graph and digest, its retained local coefficients, the first discrepancy within the common truncation, and an optional supplied factorization. Replay independently enumerates original labeled profiles, checks their energies against the nested-threshold identity, reconstructs all recorded sectors, and replays the formal Euler recomposition. The receipt records a total profile count rather than a separate count for every volume. It does not encode a q-specialization or assert an analytic continuation. Those conclusions belong to the separately stated mathematical theorem. A source digest identifies the declared graph bytes; correctness comes from the independent calculation and mathematical identities.

Replay first runs a structural parser. It rejects unknown or missing fields, non-integer or Boolean counts, negative degrees, duplicate or unsorted terms in any polynomial or marked row, rational coefficients not in lowest terms, invalid or non-canonical edges in either graph, and the superseded roadmap name relational-height/1. Only a well-formed packet reaches arithmetic. Recomputation then uses two routes, neither of which is the builder’s weak-composition engine: a replay-local stars-and-bars generator, and the level-chain search of Proposition SNG-F21. Both must reproduce the marked cells, and the work budget counts both. A packet whose counts are altered is rejected even when its digest, identity flags and every other field are left untouched. The format name, field meanings and this decision are fixed in docs/specifications/COEFFICIENTS-v1.md.

There are several different assurance levels. Direct Python enumeration is an exact finite computation relative to the interpreter and implementation. Independent enumerators reduce common implementation risk. A proof-assistant theorem about the enumeration algorithm is stronger, but does not automatically verify a particular exported table. A kernel-checked replay of the concrete table crosses that remaining boundary. Documentation should state which level each claim has reached. A schema and a future formalization plan are not present proof-assistant verification.

12.7 Analytic experiments and graph boundaries

For a first discrepancy at volume rr, a numerical prime product should evaluate the normalized ratio after extracting ζ(rs)δ\zeta(rs)^\delta, not multiply divergent raw products and interpret numerical overflow as evidence. The remainder product converges on the positive real region s>1/(r+1)s>1/(r+1) under the stated local cancellation argument. A plot near 1/r1/r should therefore compare the normalized remainder with a certified tail bound. Finite prime cutoffs need their own error estimates. Exact local coefficients establish the exponent; a fitted slope does not establish it independently.

Graph isomorphism is a separate task. Degree sequences, Laplacian spectra, binary census, and truncated height populations are filters, not general isomorphism decision procedures. Small examples can be checked by exhaustive permutation with an explicit witness or exhaustive exclusion. Larger censuses should use a documented canonical-labeling implementation and preserve its version and generation parameters. A claim that an invariant separates every graph in a census requires an independently specified complete graph population. A claim that it reconstructs all finite graphs requires a theorem. Neither follows from many successful pair comparisons.

The reproducible unit is a command, its declared finite input population, a complete output artifact, and an explanation of what that artifact proves. Small deterministic fixtures belong in routine checks. Larger censuses belong in explicit experiment scripts with resumable checkpoints and resource limits. The reference enumerator should remain available even after faster methods are introduced: its value is interpretability and independent agreement. The project becomes stronger when a reader can reproduce a modest decisive computation in minutes and then understand exactly which larger statements remain mathematical questions.

13 A mathematical research program with distinct proof routes

13.1 The question that organizes the program

The program asks how much relational information survives when labeled integer height profiles are counted by volume and quadratic edge energy, and how a first finite discrepancy becomes visible in an arithmetic Euler product. It is a question about explicit combinatorial and analytic objects. It does not require a universal theory of every obstruction, a claim that all graph information has been recovered, or an interpretation of the Euler product as a source of additional graph data. The local series supplies the data; the arithmetic product changes where and how a discrepancy is expressed.

Three levels of progress should remain distinct. A structural theorem explains an entire graph class or a transformation law. An exact counterexample separates two stated invariants. A complete finite census establishes a bounded classification relative to a documented input population. Each can support a paper, but they answer different questions. The 36 pushes in docs/development/PUSHES.md are a dependency plan for obtaining these results, not a list of results already achieved. Negative outcomes are legitimate endpoints when they are recorded with the same precision as successful separations.

13.2 Tree messages and separator geometry

Trees provide the first substantial algorithmic theorem target because conditioning on a vertex height separates the descendant subtrees. Root each component of a forest at its least original label and orient every edge from parent to child. For a vertex vv, write TvT_v for the set of descendants of vv, including vv, and E(Tv)E(T_v) for the edges with both endpoints in TvT_v. Fix a height bound H≥0H\ge0. For 0≤t≤H0\le t\le H define the message Fv(t;x,q)=∑b∈{0,…,H}Tvbv=tx∑w∈Tvbwq∑{u,w}∈E(Tv)(bu−bw)2, F_v(t;x,q)=\sum_{\substack{b\in\{0,\ldots,H\}^{T_v}\\ b_v=t}}x^{\sum_{w\in T_v}b_w}\,q^{\sum_{\{u,w\}\in E(T_v)}(b_u-b_w)^2}, a polynomial whose xmqex^mq^e coefficient counts labeled assignments of the subtree with root height tt, volume mm and internal energy ee.

Proposition SNG-F23 (forest message recursion). For every vertex vv with children u1,…,ucu_1,\ldots,u_c, $$ F_v(t)=x^t\prod_{i=1}^{c}\Bigl(\sum_{j=0}^{H}q^{(t-j)^2}F_{u_i}(j)\Bigr), $$ and the bounded-box series of the forest is CH=∏r∑t=0HFr(t)C_H=\prod_{r}\sum_{t=0}^HF_r(t), the product over component roots rr.

Proof. Induct on |Tv||T_v|. The vertex sets {v},Tu1,…,Tuc\{v\},T_{u_1},\ldots,T_{u_c} partition TvT_v, and the edges of E(Tv)E(T_v) are partitioned into the cc connecting edges {v,ui}\{v,u_i\} and the sets E(Tui)E(T_{u_i}); no other edge exists, because a forest has no edge between different child subtrees. An assignment bb on TvT_v with bv=tb_v=t is therefore the same as a choice of heights ji=buij_i=b_{u_i} and of independent assignments on each TuiT_{u_i} with root height jij_i. Its volume is tt, charged once at vv by the factor xtx^t, plus the subtree volumes; its energy is the sum of the internal subtree energies and the connecting terms (t−ji)2(t-j_i)^2, each charged once in the factor for uiu_i. Multiplication of generating polynomials realizes exactly this product of independent choices, so coefficients count labeled assignments without repetition or loss. The base case Tv={v}T_v=\{v\} gives Fv(t)=xtF_v(t)=x^t. Components are disjoint and joined by no edge, so the forest series is the product over roots of the summed root messages. ▫\square

The implementation computes messages in reverse depth-first order, so each child is complete before its parent. After FuF_u is folded into its parent it is deleted. This preserves the result because each non-root vertex has exactly one parent: no later step reads FuF_u. The roots’ messages are retained and exposed as root_messages, keyed by original labels. Three cost measures are recorded separately by transfer_statistics: height states (H+1)n(H+1)n, the total and maximum number of sparse (volume,energy)(\text{volume},\text{energy}) cells across messages, and the largest integer bit length. None is by itself a running-time bound, since sparse convolution cost depends on support products.

Proposition SNG-F24 (safe volume truncation). Let R≥0R\ge0. If every intermediate sum and product in SNG-F23, the convolution over components and the minimum-zero subtraction below are reduced by deleting monomials xmqex^mq^e with m>Rm>R, the result agrees with the unreduced computation in every coefficient with m≤Rm\le R. If H≥RH\ge R, these coefficients equal [xm]LG[x^m]L_G for m≤Rm\le R.

Proof. Deleting monomials of xx-degree above RR is the quotient map π:ℤ[q][x]→ℤ[q][x]/(xR+1)\pi:\mathbb Z[q][x]\to\mathbb Z[q][x]/(x^{R+1}), a ring homomorphism, because the monomials of degree above RR form an ideal when all xx-exponents are nonnegative: a product of a monomial of degree m>Rm>R with any polynomial of nonnegative degrees has every degree at least mm. Hence π(fg)=π(πfπg)\pi(fg)=\pi(\pi f\,\pi g) and π(f+g)=πf+πg\pi(f+g)=\pi f+\pi g, so reducing after every operation equals reducing the final answer. Multiplication by q(t−j)2q^{(t-j)^2} does not change xx-degree. Every message, the component product and CH−1C_{H-1} have nonnegative xx-exponents, which is the only property used. For the subtraction DH=CH−xnCH−1D_H=C_H-x^nC_{H-1}, the term xnCH−1x^nC_{H-1} is needed only through degree RR, so CH−1C_{H-1} is needed only through degree R−nR-n; the implementation computes it with that shifted budget. Finally, a nonnegative profile of volume m≤Rm\le R has every height at most m≤R≤Hm\le R\le H, so it lies in the box {0,…,H}n\{0,\ldots,H\}^n, and the box and unrestricted counts agree at that volume. When no budget is given the implementation uses R=nHR=nH, which deletes nothing because every box profile has volume at most nHnH. ▫\square

The argument would fail for a representation with negative volume exponents, such as a series divided by a power of xx. The retained benchmark therefore records two distinct populations: the low-volume part of an H=2H=2 box on paths of up to ninety-six vertices, which is a bounded-height population and not the unrestricted series, and H=RH=R runs on a forty-vertex ternary tree, a sixty-three-vertex binary tree and a hundred-vertex path, which compute complete unrestricted local coefficients through R=8R=8 or 1010. The latter are checked against two tree-independent identities: the profile count (m+n−1n−1)\binom{m+n-1}{n-1} and the energy sum 2|E|(m+nn+1)2|E|\binom{m+n}{n+1} at each volume, the second because ∑a(au−aw)2=2(m+nn+1)\sum_a(a_u-a_w)^2=2\binom{m+n}{n+1} over weak compositions of mm.

Proposition SNG-F25 (span by bounded-box subtraction). Let CHC_H count all profiles in {0,…,H}n\{0,\ldots,H\}^n and C−1=0C_{-1}=0. Then DH=CH−xnCH−1D_H=C_H-x^nC_{H-1} counts profiles with minimum zero and maximum at most HH, and DH−DH−1D_H-D_{H-1} (with D−1=0D_{-1}=0) counts minimum-zero profiles of span exactly HH. All counts are nonnegative.

Proof. The profiles in the box with minimum at least one are exactly b+𝟏b+\mathbf1 for b∈{0,…,H−1}nb\in\{0,\ldots,H-1\}^n. The map b↦b+𝟏b\mapsto b+\mathbf1 is a bijection, adds nn to volume and leaves energy unchanged, because every edge difference is unchanged; this is one global translation, also for disconnected graphs. Subtracting xnCH−1x^nC_{H-1} removes these and leaves the box profiles with minimum zero, a subset of the first box. A minimum-zero profile has span equal to its maximum. Minimum-zero profiles with maximum at most H−1H-1 form a subset of those with maximum at most HH, and the set difference is exactly those of span HH. Both subtractions remove the counts of a subset, so no final count is negative. For H=0H=0, D0=C0=1D_0=C_0=1 is the zero profile. ▫\square

marked_forest_coefficients implements this with the shifted budget of SNG-F24 and raises, carrying its input, if a negative difference ever appears. For every labeled forest on at most five vertices through volume five, and for named paths, stars, balanced and branched trees and a disconnected forest through volume six, its (volume,energy,span)(\text{volume},\text{energy},\text{span}) cells equal both the weak-composition and level-chain enumerators.

For general graphs, a tree decomposition replaces a single parent height by a tuple of heights on a separator. A tree decomposition of GG is a tree 𝒯\mathcal T whose nodes carry bags Xs⊆VX_s\subseteq V such that every vertex lies in some bag, both endpoints of every edge lie in a common bag, and for each vertex the bags containing it form a connected subtree. Choose a root bag. For a vertex vv the bags containing it form a subtree with a unique node nearest the root; call it the owner of vv. For an edge uvuv the bags containing both endpoints form the intersection of two subtrees, again a subtree with a unique top node, its owner. For a node ss let 𝒯s\mathcal T_s be its subtree, Vs=⋃r∈𝒯sXrV_s=\bigcup_{r\in\mathcal T_s}X_r, and WsW_s and EsE_s the vertices and edges owned by nodes of 𝒯s\mathcal T_s. For σ∈{0,…,H}Xs\sigma\in\{0,\ldots,H\}^{X_s} define Ms(σ)=∑b∈{0,…,H}Vsb|Xs=σx∑v∈Wsbvq∑uv∈Es(bu−bv)2. M_s(\sigma)=\sum_{\substack{b\in\{0,\ldots,H\}^{V_s}\\ b|_{X_s}=\sigma}}x^{\sum_{v\in W_s}b_v}q^{\sum_{uv\in E_s}(b_u-b_v)^2}.

Proposition SNG-F26 (bag-conditioned recursion). Let ws(σ)=x∑v owned by sσvq∑uv owned by s(σu−σv)2w_s(\sigma)=x^{\sum_{v\text{ owned by }s}\sigma_v}q^{\sum_{uv\text{ owned by }s}(\sigma_u-\sigma_v)^2}. Then Ms(σ)=ws(σ)∏r child of s∑τ∈{0,…,H}Xrτ|Xr∩Xs=σ|Xr∩XsMr(τ), M_s(\sigma)=w_s(\sigma)\prod_{r\text{ child of }s}\ \sum_{\substack{\tau\in\{0,\ldots,H\}^{X_r}\\ \tau|_{X_r\cap X_s}=\sigma|_{X_r\cap X_s}}}M_r(\tau), and the bounded-box series is $C_H=\sum_\sigma M_{\rm root}(\sigma)$. Every vertex volume and every edge energy is charged exactly once.

Proof. Every vertex lies in some bag and every edge in some common bag, so each has exactly one owner, and the owners partition the charges; at the root W=VW=V and $E_{\rm root}=E(G)$. Induct on |𝒯s||\mathcal T_s|. The owned sets Ws,EsW_s,E_s are the disjoint union of the charges owned at ss and the sets Wr,ErW_r,E_r of the children. A vertex v∈Vr\Xsv\in V_r\setminus X_s lies in no bag outside 𝒯r\mathcal T_r: otherwise the connected subtree of bags containing vv would pass through ss. Hence the sets Vr\XsV_r\setminus X_s for distinct children are disjoint and disjoint from XsX_s, and an assignment on VsV_s extending σ\sigma is exactly a choice, for each child independently, of an assignment on VrV_r agreeing with σ\sigma on Xr∩XsX_r\cap X_s. Every charge owned in 𝒯r\mathcal T_r involves only vertices of VrV_r, so its contribution depends only on that child’s choice. Grouping those choices by τ=b|Xr\tau=b|_{X_r} and applying the induction hypothesis gives the displayed sum for each child; the product realizes independent choices, and wsw_s adds the charges owned at ss, each once. A vertex shared by a parent and child bag carries one height because it is conditioned on both, and its volume is added only at its owner, so repeated bags and joins never double-count it. ▫\square

Safe truncation (SNG-F24) applies verbatim because every message has nonnegative volume exponents, and SNG-F25 gives the minimum-zero and exact-span sectors with one global translation. The implementation src/singularity/decomposition.py checks the decomposition axioms and the tree structure before any arithmetic and rejects a decomposition that misses a vertex or an edge or splits the bags of a vertex. Its costs are reported separately: ∑s(H+1)|Xs|\sum_s(H+1)^{|X_s|} bag assignments, sparse message support and integer bit length. On several distinct valid decompositions each of the five- and six-cycles, a ladder, K4K_4 (including redundant repeated bags), two disjoint triangles (including an empty connecting bag) and K5K_5, the bounded, minimum-zero and marked outputs equal Cartesian enumeration, weak compositions and level chains; width-one decompositions of forests, including disconnected ones, reproduce the forest engine.

13.3 What nested boundaries remember

The span-one sector records a cut-size distribution indexed by the size of a side. Span two introduces ordered nested pairs T⊆ST\subseteq S, with volume |S|+|T||S|+|T| and energy |δS|+|δT|+2e(T,V\S)|\delta S|+|\delta T|+2e(T,V\setminus S). Thus two cuts with the same individual sizes and boundary sizes can contribute differently because the graph places their boundaries differently. This is an explicit refinement mechanism. It should not be described as a higher-body interaction: the original energy remains a sum over graph edges.

A useful new intermediate object is the finite nested-pair census indexed by (|S|,|T|,|δS|,|δT|,e(T,V\S))(|S|,|T|,|\delta S|,|\delta T|,e(T,V\setminus S)). Its purpose is diagnostic. If binary-equivalent graphs first separate at span two, the census can identify which mixed boundary statistic causes that separation. Higher nested censuses are defined similarly, but their dimension grows quickly. The right theorem is not that more marks are always better; it is an explicit projection identity and, when available, a pair of graphs demonstrating that one projection loses information retained by another.

Proposition SNG-F40 (nested-pair census and its span-two projection). For a graph on VV, |V|=n|V|=n, let 𝒩G\mathcal N_G count all pairs T⊆S⊆VT\subseteq S\subseteq V, with empty, full and equal sets allowed, by (|S|,|T|,c(S),c(T),e(T,V\S))(|S|,|T|,c(S),c(T),e(T,V\setminus S)). Then: (i) 𝒩G\mathcal N_G has total mass 3n3^n; (ii) it is invariant under (s,t,cS,cT,x)↦(n−t,n−s,cT,cS,x)(s,t,c_S,c_T,x)\mapsto(n-t,n-s,c_T,c_S,x); (iii) the cells with t≥1t\ge1, s<ns<n project onto the span-two sector, [z2]ℬG(x,q,z)=∑t≥1,s<n𝒩G(s,t,cS,cT,x′)xs+tqcS+cT+2x′; [z^2]\mathcal B_G(x,q,z)=\sum_{t\ge1,\ s<n}\mathcal N_G(s,t,c_S,c_T,x')\,x^{s+t}q^{c_S+c_T+2x'}; (iv) the cells with t=0t=0 form the complete binary cut-volume census.

Proof. A pair is a choice, for each vertex, of one of the three options V\SV\setminus S, S\TS\setminus T, TT, which gives (i). The map (T,S)↦(V\S,V\T)(T,S)\mapsto(V\setminus S,V\setminus T) is an involution on nested pairs. It exchanges the two boundaries, and it preserves the crossing set: edges joining TT to V\SV\setminus S are the edges joining V\SV\setminus S to V\(V\T)V\setminus(V\setminus T). This gives (ii); on profiles it is a↦2−aa\mapsto2-a. For (iii), the pairs with ⌀≠T⊆S⊊V\varnothing\ne T\subseteq S\subsetneq V are the threshold chains of minimum-zero profiles of span two (SNG-F09 with h=2h=2), including T=ST=S for the gap profiles 2⋅𝟏S2\cdot\mathbf1_S. Volume and energy then follow from SNG-F09 and SNG-F10. Part (iv) is immediate. ▫\square

The census is strictly finer than the span-two coefficients, which see only cS+cT+2xc_S+c_T+2x. It explains the binary-census pair cell by cell. The two graphs have identical t=0t=0 cells, by (iv) and SNG-E003, yet they already differ in 591591 cells of 𝒩\mathcal N. At volume three the differing cells all have S={i,j}S=\{i,j\}, T={i}T=\{i\}, with statistics (di+dj−2Aij,di,di−Aij)(d_i+d_j-2A_{ij},\,d_i,\,d_i-A_{ij}). These are exactly the ordered adjacent-degree triples. The binary census records only the unordered sum di+dj−2Aijd_i+d_j-2A_{ij} of a two-element set, while a nested pair also orders the two vertices and records which of them is adjacent to the outside. Projecting the differing cells to energy reproduces the discrepancy polynomial q3(1−q)(1−q3)2(1−q4)2q^3(1-q)(1-q^3)^2(1-q^4)^2 of SNG-E006. The census is a finite invariant with no claimed completeness. src/singularity/nested_census.py computes it. tests/test_nested_census.py checks (i)–(iii) on all 75 labeled graphs with at most four vertices and on the reference graphs against weak compositions and level chains. results/nested_census.json retains the complete tables of the reference pairs with graph digests.

Minimum cuts provide a complementary asymptotic direction. On a connected graph, a nonconstant binary profile has positive energy, and the least such energy is the edge-connectivity. Its side-size multiplicities are visible in the marked binary sector. Nonbinary profiles can have energy tied to several nested boundaries, so identifying the first low-energy terms of the complete normalized series requires an argument about all heights. A promising target is a characterization of the minimum positive energy and its minimizing profiles, followed by a classification of the next energy layer. Each statement should distinguish energy ordering from volume ordering, since the Euler visibility theorem uses the latter.

13.4 Matroids, cut lattices, and the role of a positive chamber

The quadratic form a↦a⊤LGaa\mapsto a^\top L_Ga factors through integer height vectors modulo constants. Sending a height vector to its oriented edge differences identifies this quotient, in the connected case, with the integral cut lattice equipped with its Euclidean energy. This is established territory. The additional marks in this project are not automatically invariants of an abstract lattice: choosing the minimum-zero representative and taking its coordinate sum uses the vertex-height realization of that lattice. Span also uses that realization.

The corresponding research question is precise: which parts of BG(x,q,z)B_G(x,q,z) are determined by the metric cut lattice, which are determined by the graphic matroid, and which require additional vertex information? Whitney switches are a natural test population because they preserve cycle-matroid structure under the appropriate hypotheses. A complete search can either produce a separating pair, thereby disproving a proposed factorization through the matroid, or identify a transformation law worth proving. Failure to find a small separating pair is not proof of matroid invariance.

This path is especially useful because it can explain a collision rather than merely record one. If an equality comes from an integral lattice isometry that also preserves the chosen height chamber and marks, then a structural bijection may exist. If an isometry preserves energy but moves the chamber or the volume functional, the resulting failure identifies exactly which extra structure the series observes. The intended publication contribution would be a theorem describing such preservation or failure, with an explicit worked graph pair, rather than a broad claim that graph polynomials and lattices are connected.

13.5 Root-of-unity specializations as finite exact laboratories

Let ω\omega have order mm. Write every nonnegative height uniquely as ai=ri+mbia_i=r_i+mb_i, with 0≤ri<m0\le r_i<m. Since energy is an integer quadratic form, EG(a)≡EG(r)(modm)E_G(a)\equiv E_G(r)\pmod m. Summing the independent nonnegative bib_i gives the exact identity

LG(x,ω)=∑r∈{0,…,m−1}nx∑iriωEG(r)(1−xm)n. L_G(x,\omega)=\frac{\sum_{r\in\{0,\ldots,m-1\}^n}x^{\sum_i r_i}\omega^{E_G(r)}}{(1-x^m)^n}.

Proposition SNG-F28 (energy roots of unity give rational series). Let m≥1m\ge1 and let ω\omega be a primitive mm-th root of unity. Then LG(x,ω)=NG,m(x)/(1−xm)nL_G(x,\omega)=N_{G,m}(x)/(1-x^m)^n, where NG,m(x)=∑r∈{0,…,m−1}nx|r|ωEG(r) N_{G,m}(x)=\sum_{r\in\{0,\ldots,m-1\}^n}x^{|r|}\omega^{E_G(r)} is a polynomial of degree at most n(m−1)n(m-1) with coefficients in ℤ[ω]≅ℤ[t]/Φm(t)\mathbb Z[\omega]\cong\mathbb Z[t]/\Phi_m(t). Consequently, for every integer N≥0N\ge0, [xN]LG(x,ω)=∑0≤j≤n(m−1)j≡N(modm)[xj]NG,m⋅((N−j)/m+n−1n−1). [x^N]L_G(x,\omega)=\sum_{\substack{0\le j\le n(m-1)\\ j\equiv N\ (\mathrm{mod}\ m)}}[x^j]N_{G,m}\cdot\binom{(N-j)/m+n-1}{n-1}.

Proof. Division with remainder writes each ai≥0a_i\ge0 uniquely as ri+mbir_i+mb_i with 0≤ri<m0\le r_i<m and bi≥0b_i\ge0, so a↦(r,b)a\mapsto(r,b) is a bijection from ℤ≥0n\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^n to {0,…,m−1}n×ℤ≥0n\{0,\ldots,m-1\}^n\times\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^n with |a|=|r|+m|b||a|=|r|+m|b|. For each edge, (au−av)2=(ru−rv)2+2m(ru−rv)(bu−bv)+m2(bu−bv)2(a_u-a_v)^2=(r_u-r_v)^2+2m(r_u-r_v)(b_u-b_v)+m^2(b_u-b_v)^2, so EG(a)≡EG(r)(modm)E_G(a)\equiv E_G(r)\pmod m and ωEG(a)=ωEG(r)\omega^{E_G(a)}=\omega^{E_G(r)}. Summing over bb separately gives the factor ∑b≥0xm|b|=(1−xm)−n\sum_{b\ge0}x^{m|b|}=(1-x^m)^{-n}, whose xmkx^{mk} coefficient is the number (k+n−1n−1)\binom{k+n-1}{n-1} of weak compositions of kk into nn parts. Multiplying by NG,mN_{G,m} and reading the coefficient of xNx^N gives the remote formula, which involves only the finitely many numerator coefficients. Each ωE\omega^{E} is represented by the reduction of tEmodmt^{E\bmod m} modulo the monic integer polynomial Φm\Phi_m, so all arithmetic is exact in ℤ[t]/Φm\mathbb Z[t]/\Phi_m; for m=1m=1, Φ1=t−1\Phi_1=t-1, the ring is ℤ\mathbb Z and the formula counts all profiles. ▫\square

The identity concerns one specialization. Equality of two graphs’ specialized series at one root of unity does not imply equality of the unspecialized series: at m=2m=2 both spectral graphs have the same numerator because they have the same degree parities, although their volume-two coefficients differ, and they already differ at m=3m=3. No positivity or real-logarithm argument for 0<q<10<q<1 transfers to complex ω\omega. src/singularity/conductor.py implements NG,mN_{G,m} under an explicit residue-cube budget mnm^n and evaluates the remote formula without enumerating any height box; tests/test_conductor_weighted.py checks Φm\Phi_m against the independent product ∏d∣m(td−1)μ(m/d)\prod_{d\mid m}(t^d-1)^{\mu(m/d)} for m≤24m\le24, the numerator expansion against direct specialization of enumerated coefficients for composite orders and graphs with isolated vertices, and the retained fixtures in results/conductor_fixtures.json.

An infinite height population therefore becomes a finite residue-cube numerator at each root-of-unity specialization. This identity is a direct consequence of residue decomposition; it is not a claim of new arithmetic theory. It offers a particularly clean computational bridge because all coefficients can be represented exactly in a cyclotomic ring, and equality can be decided by reduction modulo its defining polynomial.

At q=−1q=-1, the result collapses further. Squares agree with their bases modulo two, so EG(a)≡∑idiai(mod2)E_G(a)\equiv\sum_i d_i a_i\pmod2, and

LG(x,−1)=∏i(1−(−1)dix)−1. L_G(x,-1)=\prod_i\bigl(1-(-1)^{d_i}x\bigr)^{-1}.

This specialization sees only degree parity counts. It supplies both a theorem and a warning: an elegant arithmetic specialization can discard most graph information. At odd primes, evaluating the finite numerator at x=1x=1 produces a quadratic Gauss sum for the Laplacian over a finite field. Rank and the discriminant of its nonsingular part become relevant. The singular constant direction must be accounted for, and prime powers need their own lifting argument; an odd-prime formula must not be reused at two.

There is a separate root-of-unity filter in the volume variable. Averaging LG(ωjx,q)L_G(\omega^j x,q) with character weights isolates volumes in a chosen congruence class.

Proposition SNG-F27 (volume congruence filter). Let m≥1m\ge1, let ω\omega be a primitive mm-th root of unity, let a∈ℤa\in\mathbb Z, and let F=∑v≥0Fv(q)xvF=\sum_{v\ge0}F_v(q)x^v be a formal series, or a truncation through any degree, with Fv∈ℚ[q]F_v\in\mathbb Q[q]. Then 1m∑j=0m−1ω−ajF(ωjx,q)=∑v≡a(modm)Fv(q)xv. \frac1m\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}\omega^{-aj}F(\omega^jx,q)=\sum_{v\equiv a\ (\mathrm{mod}\ m)}F_v(q)x^v .

Proof. The coefficient of xvx^v on the left is Fv(q)⋅1m∑j=0m−1ζjF_v(q)\cdot\frac1m\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}\zeta^{j} with ζ=ωv−a\zeta=\omega^{v-a}. If v≡a(modm)v\equiv a\pmod m, then ζ=1\zeta=1 and the average is 11. Otherwise ζ≠1\zeta\ne1 and ζm=1\zeta^m=1, so (ζ−1)∑jζj=ζm−1=0(\zeta-1)\sum_j\zeta^j=\zeta^m-1=0 forces ∑jζj=0\sum_j\zeta^j=0; this holds in the field ℚ(ω)≅ℚ[t]/Φm(t)\mathbb Q(\omega)\cong\mathbb Q[t]/\Phi_m(t), hence in the integral representation ℤ[t]/Φm(t)\mathbb Z[t]/\Phi_m(t). The identity is coefficientwise, so it holds for every truncation and for any residue representative aa; for m=1m=1 it is the identity map. ▫\square

The implementation in src/singularity/congruence.py evaluates the left side literally in ℤ[t]/Φm(t)\mathbb Z[t]/\Phi_m(t), including the nonprimitive powers ωj\omega^j, divides only the completed sum by mm, and raises if the sum is not an integer multiple of the identity. Tests compare it with direct degree selection and with tuple enumeration filtered by each profile’s own volume on all labeled graphs with at most four vertices, for several moduli including composite ones and truncations shorter than the modulus. The filter acts on the volume variable; the energy specialization q=ωq=\omega above is a different operation. It does not isolate binary profiles or recover span after setting z=1z=1: volume classes merge different spans with equal volume and energy, as 2ei2e_i and ei+eje_i+e_j on an edgeless graph already show. Both kinds of specialization are worthwhile because they provide finite exact comparison problems with different information loss. The positive-real visibility theorem for 0<q<10<q<1 does not automatically extend to complex qq, where local factors may vanish and a logarithm needs an explicitly chosen domain.

13.6 Order chambers and weighted lattice-point geometry

Every height profile has a unique order obtained by sorting vertices first by height and then by label. For a permutation π\pi in that order, introduce d0=aπ1d_0=a_{\pi_1} and dj=aπj+1−aπjd_j=a_{\pi_{j+1}}-a_{\pi_j} for 1≤j<n1\le j<n. These gaps are nonnegative, with dj>0d_j>0 whenever πj>πj+1\pi_j>\pi_{j+1}, because an adjacent descent cannot occur inside a tied block. The resulting chambers are disjoint, including their prescribed boundaries. Volume becomes nd0+∑j=1n−1(n−j)djnd_0+\sum_{j=1}^{n-1}(n-j)d_j, and energy becomes an explicit quadratic form in the remaining gaps.

Proposition SNG-F29 (disjoint order chambers). Index positions from 00. For a permutation π=(π0,…,πn−1)\pi=(\pi_0,\ldots,\pi_{n-1}) let CπC_\pi be the set of gap vectors d∈ℤ≥0nd\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^n with dj≥1d_j\ge1 whenever j≥1j\ge1 and πj−1>πj\pi_{j-1}>\pi_j. The map (π,d)↦a(\pi,d)\mapsto a, aπk=d0+⋯+dka_{\pi_k}=d_0+\cdots+d_k, is a bijection from ⨆πCπ\bigsqcup_\pi C_\pi onto ℤ≥0n\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^n. Writing Tj={πj,…,πn−1}T_j=\{\pi_j,\ldots,\pi_{n-1}\}, |a|=nd0+∑j=1n−1(n−j)dj,EG(a)=∑i,j=1n−1Qijdidj,Qjj=cG(Tj),Qij=eG(Tmax(i,j),V\Tmin(i,j)), |a|=nd_0+\sum_{j=1}^{n-1}(n-j)d_j,\qquad E_G(a)=\sum_{i,j=1}^{n-1}Q_{ij}d_id_j,\qquad Q_{jj}=c_G(T_j),\quad Q_{ij}=e_G\bigl(T_{\max(i,j)},V\setminus T_{\min(i,j)}\bigr), and on d0=0d_0=0 (the normalized profiles) the span is ∑j≥1dj\sum_{j\ge1}d_j.

Proof. Given aa, let π\pi list the vertices by increasing (av,v)(a_v,v) and set d0=aπ0d_0=a_{\pi_0}, dj=aπj−aπj−1d_j=a_{\pi_j}-a_{\pi_{j-1}}. The gaps are nonnegative, and if πj−1>πj\pi_{j-1}>\pi_j the two heights cannot be equal, because equal heights are sorted by increasing label; so d∈Cπd\in C_\pi and the map hits aa. Conversely, for d∈Cπd\in C_\pi the heights aπka_{\pi_k} are nondecreasing in kk, and two consecutive positions tie only when dj=0d_j=0, which forces πj−1<πj\pi_{j-1}<\pi_j. Sorting aa by (av,v)(a_v,v) therefore returns π\pi, and the gaps are recovered by differences, so (π,d)(\pi,d) is determined by aa: the chambers are disjoint. Vertex πk\pi_k has height d0+⋯+dkd_0+\cdots+d_k, so gap djd_j is counted at the n−jn-j positions k≥jk\ge j, giving the volume. An edge with endpoints at positions p<qp<q has difference dp+1+⋯+dqd_{p+1}+\cdots+d_q; squaring and summing over edges gives ∑Qijdidj\sum Q_{ij}d_id_j, where QijQ_{ij} counts edges whose position interval contains both ii and jj. Such an edge has its upper endpoint in Tmax(i,j)T_{\max(i,j)} and its lower endpoint outside Tmin(i,j)T_{\min(i,j)}, and conversely; for i=ji=j this is the cut of TjT_j. The minimum height is d0d_0 and the maximum d0+∑j≥1djd_0+\sum_{j\ge1}d_j. ▫\square

The matrix QQ is the nested-boundary matrix of SNG-F10 for the chain T1⊇⋯⊇Tn−1T_1\supseteq\cdots\supseteq T_{n-1}, with gap djd_j recording how many threshold levels coincide with TjT_j. Closed weak-order cones would place a profile with a tied block of size ss in s!s! cones; the strict descent condition removes exactly that overcount. src/singularity/chambers.py enumerates the n!n! chambers and their gap vectors within a volume budget, evaluates volume and energy from QQ, and never constructs height tuples; its factorial cost restricts it to small graphs. Its local and marked histograms equal the weak-composition and level-chain enumerators on all 75 labeled graphs with at most four vertices through volume six, and the chamber of every profile in {0,…,3}4\{0,\ldots,3\}^4 is recovered uniquely.

This description links the population to familiar order and lattice-point methods while retaining a concrete accounting benefit. It can expose which cross terms depend on the relative placement of cuts, and it gives another independent enumerator. The marks are not automatically Ehrhart polynomials. Unweighted integer points in a dilated fixed rational polytope admit established Ehrhart theory; weighting them by qq to a quadratic energy introduces an additional structure. Any reciprocity statement must specify whether it concerns unweighted counts, a formal weighted series, or a transformed analytic function, and must prove the claimed boundary terms.

Proposition SNG-F32 (poset-constrained heights and order polytopes). Let PP be a finite poset on VV, |V|=n|V|=n, and 𝒪(P)={x∈[0,1]n:xi≤xj whenever i<Pj}\mathcal O(P)=\{x\in[0,1]^n:x_i\le x_j\text{ whenever }i<_Pj\}, with the inequalities oriented as in the height constraint. For every integer H≥0H\ge0:

  1. The weak assignments a∈{0,…,H}na\in\{0,\ldots,H\}^n with ai≤aja_i\le a_j for i<Pji<_Pj are exactly the lattice points of H𝒪(P)H\mathcal O(P). Their number is Ω(P,H+1)\Omega(P,H+1), where Ω(P,m)\Omega(P,m) is Stanley’s order polynomial, which counts order-preserving maps P→{1,…,m}P\to\{1,\ldots,m\}. For any natural labeling, Ω(P,H+1)=∑σ∈ℒ(P)(H+n−desσn)\Omega(P,H+1)=\sum_{\sigma\in\mathcal L(P)}\binom{H+n-\operatorname{des}\sigma}{n}.
  2. In the chamber decomposition of SNG-F29, a relation i<Pji<_Pj holds automatically when ii precedes jj in the chamber order. When ii follows jj, it forces every gap between them to be zero, which is impossible across a label descent. Each surviving chamber contributes (H−s+ff)\binom{H-s+f}{f} points, where ff counts free gaps and ss is the forced minimum.
  3. Strict assignments, with ai<aja_i<a_j, form a different population. For a chain they number (H+1n)\binom{H+1}{n} instead of (H+nn)\binom{H+n}{n}.
  4. The weighted count ∑a∈H𝒪(P)∩ℤnx|a|qEG(a)\sum_{a\in H\mathcal O(P)\cap\mathbb Z^n}x^{|a|}q^{E_G(a)} is a finite weighted sum over the same points. For fixed 0<q<10<q<1 it need not be a polynomial in HH.

Proof. (1) Scaling 𝒪(P)\mathcal O(P) by HH gives 0≤xi≤H0\le x_i\le H and the same order inequalities, so its integer points are the weak assignments. The map a↦a+𝟏a\mapsto a+\mathbf1 identifies them with order-preserving maps to {1,…,H+1}\{1,\ldots,H+1\}, which is the argument shift. For a natural labeling, each weak map lies in exactly one chamber of SNG-F29 (sorting by height and then label), and the chambers it can occupy are exactly the linear extensions, since ties are broken by increasing label and a natural labeling increases along relations. In the chamber of σ\sigma, the gaps d1,…,dn−1d_1,\ldots,d_{n-1} are at least one at the desσ\operatorname{des}\sigma descents. The points with maximum at most HH correspond to nonnegative solutions of ∑j≥0dj′≤H−desσ\sum_{j\ge0}d_j'\le H-\operatorname{des}\sigma, which number (H−desσ+nn)\binom{H-\operatorname{des}\sigma+n}{n}. (2) is the same count without assuming a natural labeling. If ii precedes jj the heights are nondecreasing along the order. If ii follows jj, then ai≥aja_i\ge a_j, so the relation requires equality and every intermediate gap must vanish. (3) A strict chain assignment chooses nn distinct values in {0,…,H}\{0,\ldots,H\}. (4) For the two-element chain with the edge {0,1}\{0,1\}, the weighted count is WH(q)=∑d=0H(H+1−d)qd2W_H(q)=\sum_{d=0}^H(H+1-d)q^{d^2}. Its second difference in HH is q(H+2)2q^{(H+2)^2}, which is positive and tends to 00. The second difference of a polynomial is a polynomial, and one that tends to 00 vanishes identically, so WHW_H is not a polynomial in HH. The unweighted count on the same points is the polynomial (H+22)\binom{H+2}2. ▫\square

Statement (1) is classical [Stanley1986; Stanley2012]. The project adds two things: the chamber form (2), which applies to arbitrary labels and is checked against direct enumeration, and the explicit warning (4). Quadratic weighting keeps the lattice points of the order polytope but leaves the polynomial world of ordinary Ehrhart theory, so a reciprocity statement for weighted counts needs its own proof (P22). src/singularity/orders.py validates acyclicity and takes the transitive closure. Its direct, chamber and linear-extension counts agree on chains, a reversed chain, antichains, the diamond, a poset with unnatural labels, a disconnected poset and a redundant relation for several complete height ranges.

Two reciprocity statements hold for these counts, and both are established background rather than project results [Stanley2012]. For strict assignments ai<aja_i<a_j with values in {0,…,H}\{0,\ldots,H\}, the count is (−1)nΩ(P,−(H+1))(-1)^n\Omega(P,-(H+1)), where Ω(P,m)\Omega(P,m) is the order polynomial of SNG-F32 evaluated as a polynomial at a negative integer. For unbounded heights, let WP(x)=∑x|a|W_P(x)=\sum x^{|a|} over weak maps a≥0a\ge0 and SP(x)=∑x|a|S_P(x)=\sum x^{|a|} over strict maps a≥1a\ge1. Both are rational. In chamber form, with ties broken by increasing natural label for WW and by decreasing natural label for SS, WP=∑σ∈ℒ(P)x∑j∈Desσ(n−j)∏i=1n(1−xi),SP=∑σ∈ℒ(P)xn+∑j∈Ascσ(n−j)∏i=1n(1−xi), W_P=\frac{\sum_{\sigma\in\mathcal L(P)}x^{\sum_{j\in\operatorname{Des}\sigma}(n-j)}}{\prod_{i=1}^n(1-x^i)},\qquad S_P=\frac{\sum_{\sigma\in\mathcal L(P)}x^{\,n+\sum_{j\in\operatorname{Asc}\sigma}(n-j)}}{\prod_{i=1}^n(1-x^i)}, and SP(x)=(−1)nWP(1/x)S_P(x)=(-1)^nW_P(1/x). Breaking ties by decreasing label makes every tied block a decreasing run of a linear extension, hence an antichain. This is exactly what strictness permits. The two exponents add to n(n+1)/2n(n+1)/2, which gives the identity.

Theorem SNG-F34 (energy weights obstruct P-partition reciprocity). Let PP be the two-element chain 0<10<1 and G=K2G=K_2 on the same vertices, and put W(x,q)=∑0≤a0≤a1xa0+a1q(a1−a0)2W(x,q)=\sum_{0\le a_0\le a_1}x^{a_0+a_1}q^{(a_1-a_0)^2} and S(x,q)=∑1≤a0<a1xa0+a1q(a1−a0)2S(x,q)=\sum_{1\le a_0<a_1}x^{a_0+a_1}q^{(a_1-a_0)^2}. Then W=θ(x,q)1−x2,S=x2(θ(x,q)−1)1−x2,θ(x,q)=∑d≥0xdqd2, W=\frac{\theta(x,q)}{1-x^2},\qquad S=\frac{x^2(\theta(x,q)-1)}{1-x^2},\qquad \theta(x,q)=\sum_{d\ge0}x^dq^{d^2}, and neither WW nor SS is a rational function of xx over ℚ(q)\mathbb Q(q). Consequently W(1/x,⋅)W(1/x,\cdot) has no meaning as a rational function, and no identity of the form S(x,q)=±W(1/x,ψ(q))S(x,q)=\pm W(1/x,\psi(q)) extends the classical reciprocity, which holds at q=1q=1.

Proof. Writing a=(t,t+d)a=(t,t+d) gives the closed forms. If WW were rational in xx over ℚ(q)\mathbb Q(q), so would be θ=(1−x2)W\theta=(1-x^2)W. Its coefficients qd2q^{d^2} would then satisfy a linear recurrence ∑i=0kciq(d+i)2=0\sum_{i=0}^kc_iq^{(d+i)^2}=0 for all d≥d0d\ge d_0, with ci∈ℚ(q)c_i\in\mathbb Q(q) not all zero. Dividing by qd2q^{d^2} gives ∑iciqi2yi=0\sum_ic_iq^{i^2}y^i=0 with y=q2dy=q^{2d}. This polynomial in yy would vanish at the infinitely many distinct elements q2dq^{2d} of ℚ(q)\mathbb Q(q), hence identically, forcing every ci=0c_i=0. The same argument applies to SS. At q=1q=1, θ=1/(1−x)\theta=1/(1-x), W=1/((1−x)(1−x2))W=1/((1-x)(1-x^2)) and S=x3/((1−x)(1−x2))=W(1/x)S=x^3/((1-x)(1-x^2))=W(1/x). ▫\square

The obstruction concerns rationality in xx, which the classical proof needs. It does not rule out other weighted identities with additional boundary terms or a transformed analytic function; any such claim would need its own definition of the evaluation at 1/x1/x or at negative bounds. The bounded weighted count is not polynomial in HH either (SNG-F32), so evaluation at negative HH is also undefined. tests/test_reciprocity.py checks both background reciprocities on six complete small posets, including singleton, chain, antichain, diamond, unnatural labeling and a disconnected poset. It checks the closed forms of WW and SS through x12x^{12} by direct enumeration and confirms that the Hankel determinants det[q(i+j)2]0≤i,j≤k\det[q^{(i+j)^2}]_{0\le i,j\le k} for k≤3k\le3 are nonzero polynomials. These determinants are the finite certificates excluding recurrences of order kk that start at d=0d=0.

The intended order-theoretic theorem target is a chamber formula with a correct treatment of ties, followed by reductions for graph families with a controlled set of chamber types. An algorithm summing all n!n! orders may be a useful check without being a useful large-scale algorithm. A later symmetry reduction must preserve the original labeled multiplicities. Successful chamber identities would provide exact explanations for some coefficient factorizations, rather than relying on numerical pattern recognition.

13.7 Visibility strata and formal proof priorities

For fixed graph pairs, coefficient differences are polynomials in qq. Their common vanishing defines exceptional parameter values where the first discrepancy moves to a later volume. The generic first discrepancy and its exceptional set should be computed separately. At a rational parameter, direct substitution determines whether a proposed exponent survives. At an algebraic parameter, reduction by a minimal polynomial gives an exact test. Sampling several real values cannot prove that a discrepancy has no interior zero.

Proposition SNG-F31 (exceptional strata are finite and exactly computable). Let Δv=[xv](LG−LH)∈ℤ[q]\Delta_v=[x^v](L_G-L_H)\in\mathbb Z[q] for 0≤v≤R0\le v\le R, let rr be the least vv with Δv≠0\Delta_v\ne0, and for q0∈(0,1)q_0\in(0,1) let r(q0)r(q_0) be the least v≤Rv\le R with Δv(q0)≠0\Delta_v(q_0)\ne0, if any. Then r(q0)=rr(q_0)=r except at the finitely many roots of Δr\Delta_r in (0,1)(0,1); at such a root α\alpha, r(q0)r(q_0) is the least v>rv>r with Δv(α)≠0\Delta_v(\alpha)\ne0, or undefined through RR. Every such root is found by Sturm isolation of the square-free part of Δr\Delta_r, and whether Δv(α)=0\Delta_v(\alpha)=0 is decided exactly.

Proof. For v<rv<r, Δv=0\Delta_v=0 identically, so r(q0)≥rr(q_0)\ge r for every q0q_0, with equality exactly when Δr(q0)≠0\Delta_r(q_0)\ne0. A nonzero polynomial has finitely many roots. Let f=Δr/gcd(Δr,Δr′)f=\Delta_r/\gcd(\Delta_r,\Delta_r'), which has the same roots, all simple. Sturm’s theorem states that the number of distinct roots of ff in (a,b](a,b] equals the drop in sign changes of its Sturm sequence from aa to bb; subtracting a root at bb, found by exact evaluation, gives the number strictly inside. Bisection at rational midpoints, recording any midpoint that is a root, splits every interval with two or more roots. It terminates because distinct roots are separated by a positive distance. Each surviving interval then contains exactly one root, so the list is complete. For an isolated root α\alpha of ff in (a,b)(a,b), Δv(α)=0\Delta_v(\alpha)=0 if and only if α\alpha is a common root of ff and Δv\Delta_v, that is, a root of gcd(f,Δv)\gcd(f,\Delta_v). That gcd divides ff, so its roots in (a,b)(a,b) are among those of ff, namely α\alpha alone, and a Sturm count of the gcd on the interval decides the question. Rational arithmetic is exact throughout. ▫\square

src/singularity/parameters.py implements this. It reports rational roots exactly, also through the rational-root theorem when the coefficients are small. It represents the others by a square-free defining polynomial and an isolating interval. The defining polynomial divides a discrepancy and need not be the minimal polynomial. It also computes multiplicities by repeated derivatives and evaluates the endpoints q=0,1q=0,1 separately. For the spectral, binary-census and cube–Möbius pairs it finds no interior root of the leading discrepancy, so the first visible volume is 22, 33 and 44 at every q∈(0,1)q\in(0,1) (results/parameter_strata.json). At both endpoints the binary pair agrees through the tested bound. Artificial discrepancies with interior irrational and rational roots, repeated roots and identically zero differences are tested as well.

The analytic path starts with a finite certified coefficient discrepancy, then proves a local factor expansion and a uniformly convergent normalized prime product in the stated real domain. More cancellations can move the remainder convergence boundary; they do not justify a global meromorphic continuation of the original product. Nonintegral exponents require positive-real branches or explicitly described local complex branches. The project should seek quantitative remainder bounds uniform on compact parameter intervals away from exceptional points, so numerical demonstrations become reproducible approximations to an already stated theorem.

Formalization should follow the dependency order of the mathematics. First prove finite graph energy definitions, translation normalization, binary extraction, and the nested-level identity. Next verify finite coefficient tables and polynomial discrepancy certificates. Only then formalize the analytic comparison theorem against whatever zeta and infinite-product library is actually available. If a library theorem is assumed or imported externally, state that boundary. The central objective is a short chain from an explicit labeled population to a specific real singularity, with every link visible to a reader and no broader reconstruction or formal-verification claim added by implication.

14 Literature, attribution, and publication claims

14.1 The contribution must be stated at the right scale

The ingredients of this project have substantial precedents. Graph Laplacians, integer cut lattices, Ising partition functions, Gaussian fields, order polytopes, Euler transforms, and zeta-factor extraction are established mathematics. Combining their names is not a novelty claim. A defensible contribution must identify a specific population, a theorem about information retained by its particular marks, a verified separation from a stated invariant, a new algorithm with a correctness argument, or a classification result that was not already supplied by the background literature.

The present formulation counts nonnegative labeled vertex heights by total height and squared edge differences, with an optional minimum-zero normalization and span mark. Its immediate value is that this object supports a short exact route from finite profiles to an arithmetic comparison. That route is worth explaining even when individual steps are elementary. Whether the resulting invariant, a specific identity, or a particular example has historical priority remains a literature question. The repository should claim what it establishes, not use the absence of a familiar name as evidence of originality.

There is also a distinction between mathematical novelty and a useful research artifact. A reproducible pair of examples with explicit edges, exact coefficient maps, an independent implementation, and a readable proof can be valuable without being advertised as a new general theory. A literature-ready manuscript should explain the closest known objects first, then state the narrower result. It should give readers enough detail to decide whether the distinction is substantial. Publication merit is strengthened by a theorem that explains a family of examples, rather than by a larger vocabulary around one computation.

14.2 Binary heights and the established Ising polynomial

Define the complete binary census by CG(u,v)=∑S⊆Vu|S|v|δS|C_G(u,v)=\sum_{S\subseteq V}u^{|S|}v^{|\delta S|}. This is a conventional form of a bivariate Ising polynomial. With spins σi∈{−1,1}\sigma_i\in\{-1,1\}, take SS to be the negative-spin set. Then ∑iσi=n−2|S|\sum_i\sigma_i=n-2|S| and ∑{i,j}∈Eσiσj=|E|−2|δS|\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E}\sigma_i\sigma_j=|E|-2|\delta S|. The standard Ising partition sum with uniform coupling and field is therefore eβ|E|+hnCG(e−2h,e−2β)e^{\beta|E|+hn}C_G(e^{-2h},e^{-2\beta}), under this sign convention. This change of variables should accompany comparisons with the literature; polynomial names alone can conceal differing normalizations.

Andrén and Markström studied the bivariate Ising polynomial explicitly. Sokal’s account of the multivariate Tutte polynomial explains the larger Potts and matroid setting. Neither reference justifies claiming that every multilevel integer-height population is determined by the binary census. The supplied binary-census pair provides an exact finite separation in the opposite direction for this particular series. The appropriate statement is that these two specified graphs have equal binary census and unequal height coefficients, with the precise certificate supplied. It is not that the project first discovered that distinct graphs can share an Ising polynomial.

The span mark clarifies the information relation. The full marked normalized series contains the nonconstant binary census at span one. The unmarked specialization sums all spans together. No recovery theorem for the binary sector from that specialization has been established here. This boundary belongs in a paper because it distinguishes a proved inclusion of information from a plausible but unproved relationship between two projections.

14.3 Cut lattices, spectra, and Gaussian comparisons

Bacher, de la Harpe, and Nagnibeda develop the integral flow and cut lattices associated with graphs. Their work is a direct antecedent for interpreting squared edge differences as a lattice energy. In a connected graph, integer heights modulo constants map to integral edge gradients; changing an edge orientation changes signs of coordinates, not the energy. A manuscript should cite this framework before discussing its additional chamber and volume marks. The existence of a cut-lattice description is background, while any theorem describing which of these additional marks survive a lattice isometry is a separate contribution requiring proof.

The usual continuous Gaussian integral on the zero-mean subspace depends only on the nonzero Laplacian eigenvalues. For example, integrating exp(−tx⊤LGx)\exp(-t x^\top L_Gx) with Euclidean measure on that subspace gives π(n−1)/2t−(n−1)/2/det′LG\pi^{(n-1)/2}t^{-(n-1)/2}/\sqrt{\det' L_G}. This makes cospectrality a natural comparison, but does not imply that every discrete Gaussian or lattice theta series is spectral. Integrality, a positive-height chamber, and a volume mark retain additional structure. The distinction is classical in spirit and should not be presented as a discovery that continuous spectra can lose combinatorial information.

Rue and Held provide an authoritative account of Gaussian Markov random fields and precision-matrix methods. Their subject helps explain why Laplacians appear, not why this specific height series must be novel. The spectral example in this repository establishes a concrete strict comparison with the Laplacian characteristic polynomial on the given graph pair. A statement about all graph spectra, all lattice theta functions, or complete reconstruction would go beyond that evidence.

14.4 Orders, matroids, and Euler products

Stanley’s order-polytope and chain-polytope theory is relevant when height inequalities are organized by partial orders. His work on acyclic orientations is relevant when edge directions are induced by vertex orders. The project should use these theories where their hypotheses actually hold. A finite height box can be decomposed into ordered chambers; this does not make a quadratic-energy weighted sum an ordinary Ehrhart polynomial. A claimed reciprocity theorem must specify its weights, strictness convention, and boundary strata. An analogy with a familiar theorem is a guide to a proof, not a substitute for one.

The matroid question likewise needs a precise target. Sokal treats graph and matroid partition functions, while cut-lattice theory supplies another route to graph equivalences. A relational height series may retain information about the vertex realization that a matroid forgets. To establish this, one should either produce a certified pair related by an appropriate matroid-preserving operation and separated by the series, or prove a transformation theorem. Neither the phrase ‘matroid refinement’ nor a generic graph collision is sufficient.

Euler transforms and Möbius inversion explain how local formal coefficients can be reorganized into cyclotomic factors. For a scalar formal series A(x)∈1+xK[[x]]A(x)\in1+xK[[x]], with KK of characteristic zero, write logA(x)=∑n≥1cnxn\log A(x)=\sum_{n\ge1}c_nx^n. There are unique formal exponents bn∈Kb_n\in K with A(x)=∏n≥1(1−xn)−bnA(x)=\prod_{n\ge1}(1-x^n)^{-b_n}, and ncn=∑d∣ndbdn c_n=\sum_{d\mid n}d b_d. Moree’s work on the formal series Witt transform is a relevant account of the associated cyclotomic identities and Möbius transforms. When qq is a parameter, scalar exponents need not be nonnegative integers or even integer-coefficient polynomials in qq.

The analytic Euler product requires a separate argument. Extracting finitely many zeta factors can improve the convergence of a remainder, but a formal infinite factorization is not automatically a global analytic continuation. In this project, the first-discrepancy statement uses a finite local expansion and a normalized remainder converging in a specified region. With a nonintegral discrepancy exponent, a real positive branch is available; a blanket meromorphic-continuation claim is not. The arithmetic lift reexpresses local information and supplies a singularity comparison. It does not increase the invariant’s graph-reconstruction power.

14.5 A claim register for papers and releases

An established-background claim should name its source and retain its hypotheses. A proved proposition should have a complete argument in the manuscript, with graph order, connectedness, and parameter restrictions visible. An exact finite claim should give the finite input population and a reproducible coefficient or graph certificate. A conjecture should be phrased so that a counterexample or a proof can settle it. A proposed algorithm should not be described as implemented until its code and validation are present. These categories are editorial tools for keeping a mathematical narrative honest, rather than an additional software framework.

For the current examples, acceptable language is: ‘For the two graphs with the displayed edge lists, the Laplacian characteristic polynomials agree, while the local height series first differ at volume two by the displayed polynomial.’ The binary example has the analogous finite census statement and a first difference at volume three. If independent enumeration has been run, that fact can be added with its method. ‘The invariant reconstructs graphs,’ ‘all graphs were checked,’ ‘the proof is kernel verified,’ and ‘this is the first such invariant’ require evidence of a different kind and should be absent unless that evidence is supplied.

The strongest candidate conjectures concern explicit comparison boundaries: whether a marked series factors through a given lattice or matroid structure, whether a specified family has a bounded first-separation volume, or whether a nested-cut hierarchy is strict at arbitrarily many levels. An exhaustive finite experiment can guide these conjectures and may disprove them. It cannot establish an unrestricted theorem. If a proposed direction reproduces an already known object after a change of variables, the correct outcome is an attribution and a revised question.

14.6 Candidate paper abstracts with stated prerequisites

Candidate A: Relational height populations and arithmetic visibility. The following abstract is suitable only when the finite examples and analytic comparison have their full proofs and released certificates: ‘We study labeled nonnegative integer heights on a finite graph, weighted by total height and quadratic edge energy. Translation normalization gives minimum-zero representatives, and a span marking resolves nested boundary contributions. Explicit graph pairs separate this population from the Laplacian spectrum and from a complete binary cut census. For a fixed real energy parameter, we show that the first differing local coefficient determines a zeta-factor exponent in the ratio of the associated prime products. The remainder is controlled in a specified real convergence region. The examples and coefficient identities are supplied with exact reproducible data.’ This abstract claims no general reconstruction theorem or historical priority.

Candidate B: Exact height enumeration on trees and bounded separators. This is a future methods paper, conditional on the dynamic programs, correctness proofs, and measured experiments being completed: ‘We develop exact volume-truncated algorithms for graph height populations using separator-conditioned generating functions. A bounded-height formulation recovers minimum-zero and span-marked coefficients by translation subtraction. Independent composition and level-chain enumerators establish finite reference data, and exact ranking provides reproducible conditioned witnesses. We analyze state growth and polynomial-convolution costs separately and compare complete coefficient ranges on tree and bounded-width families.’ Speedups and maximum instance sizes must be inserted from actual measurements, not anticipated results.

Candidate C: What graph structure survives a height population? This is a structural question rather than an available result: ‘We compare marked integer-height populations with metric cut lattices and graph matroids, identifying transformation laws and explicit obstructions to preservation of the volume chamber.’ A paper with this abstract needs an actual theorem or a decisive classification. The current program supplies the question and test apparatus. It does not yet supply the answer. A negative result showing that a proposed refinement collapses to known data would also be publishable if its statement and proof are substantive.

14.7 Verified references and their intended use

Roland Bacher, Pierre de la Harpe, and Tatiana Nagnibeda, ‘The lattice of integral flows and the lattice of integral cuts on a finite graph,’ Bulletin de la Société Mathématique de France 125 (1997), 167–198. DOI: 10.24033/bsmf.2303. The Numdam record and article provide the primary source. Use this for the established lattice setting, not as an attribution for the particular marked series defined here.

Daniel Andrén and Klas Markström, ‘The bivariate Ising polynomial of a graph,’ Discrete Applied Mathematics 157 (2009), 2515–2524. DOI: 10.1016/j.dam.2009.02.021. Use this for the binary comparison and for checking normalization conventions. Equality of a binary census is an established equivalence relation; its failure to determine this particular multilevel series is the narrower issue tested here.

Alan D. Sokal, ‘The multivariate Tutte polynomial (alias Potts model) for graphs and matroids,’ in Surveys in Combinatorics 2005, 173–226. Primary author manuscript: arXiv:math/0503607. Use this for partition-function and matroid background. The document explicitly addresses the flexibility of multivariate weights; any claim of improvement must compare actual specializations and information, rather than compare names.

Håvard Rue and Leonhard Held, Gaussian Markov Random Fields: Theory and Applications, Chapman & Hall/CRC, 2005. DOI: 10.1201/9780203492024. The publisher record verifies authorship and edition. Use this for Gaussian precision-matrix context; the elementary restricted Gaussian integral should still be derived with the measure convention used in the manuscript.

Richard P. Stanley, ‘Two poset polytopes,’ Discrete & Computational Geometry 1 (1986), 9–23. DOI: 10.1007/BF02187680. The author-hosted article is the primary accessible text. Use this for order and chain polytopes and their lattice-point interpretation, with a separate proof for any quadratic-energy extension.

Richard P. Stanley, ‘Acyclic orientations of graphs,’ Discrete Mathematics 5 (1973), 171–178. DOI: 10.1016/0012-365X(73)90108-8. The 2006 reprint has a different DOI; cite the original year when discussing the original theorem. Use this for the classical orientation and reciprocity background, not for a weighted identity that has not been established.

Pieter Moree, ‘The formal series Witt transform,’ Discrete Mathematics 295 (2005), 143–160. DOI: 10.1016/j.disc.2005.03.004. The author’s institutional publication record supplies an accessible description and published version. Use this for formal cyclotomic and Möbius-transform context. The real analytic remainder argument in this project must be stated and proved independently.

Brendan D. McKay and Adolfo Piperno, ‘Practical graph isomorphism, II,’ Journal of Symbolic Computation 60 (2014), 94–112. DOI: 10.1016/j.jsc.2013.09.003. Primary author manuscript: arXiv:1301.1493. Use this when a census relies on canonical labeling or on nauty/Traces. A citation does not substitute for recording the actual executable version, graph-generation command, and completeness boundary of a particular experiment.

These references were checked against primary author, publisher, or journal records for this release. They are a starting bibliography, not a completed priority search. Before journal submission, the author should search directly for integer-valued graph Gaussian models, graph height partition functions, multivariate theta series, and refinements of Ising-equivalent graphs, then compare definitions term by term. A responsible priority statement belongs at the end of that process.

15 Implementation and retained computational results

The mathematical manuscripts describe a research program, while this chapter records the executable boundary of version 0.1.0. The core package requires Python 3.10 or newer and uses only the standard library. Documentation generation additionally uses Pandoc and a LaTeX installation. The rendered PDF and HTML are distributed so that a reader does not need those authoring tools merely to read the work.

15.1 Installing and running the project

From the repository root, python -m pip install -e . installs the command singularity. An installation-free alternative is to set PYTHONPATH=src and invoke python -m singularity. The commands emit structured JSON so a retained calculation can be consumed by another experiment. Human explanations and proofs live in the monograph; JSON field names are not intended to replace the mathematical exposition.

python -m singularity examples prints the four original seven-vertex sources. python -m singularity compare binary_g binary_h --max-volume 3 recovers their binary-census equality and first local difference. The parameter --q 1/2 uses an exact rational, and the reported value is an exact fraction. A vanishing specialization is reported without pretending that a symbolic discrepancy remained visible at that parameter.

python -m singularity profile --example binary_g --max-volume 4 returns the degree data, exact Laplacian polynomial, binary census, local coefficients, normalized coefficients and marked height sectors. The input can instead be a JSON object with an integer vertex count and an explicit edge list. Original vertex labels are retained throughout all finite populations. Isomorphism is a separate mathematical quotient, never an implicit division of multiplicities.

15.2 Implemented mathematical modules

The meaning of every public coefficient, population and certificate interface is fixed in the coefficient specification. The finite graph population used by census comparisons is fixed in the census specification.
